items.title: Wrexham face Liverpool with Premier League still in their sights despite setback | Wrexham | The Guardian
items.summary:
Parkinson’s team face Liverpool with confidence in the Bronx on Wednesday having defeated Manchester United and Leeds in pre-season so far and moved on from the anguish of missing out on the Championship playoffs on the final day of last season. The near-miss was undoubtedly a setback to an ambitious club’s grand vision but finishing seventh in the Championship at the first time of asking, Parkinson insists, was an accomplishment that should not be dismissed lightly. [...] The Wrexham co-owner Ryan Reynolds called it a “punch-me moment” – his club playing Liverpool in a pre-season friendly at Yankee Stadium just five years after he and Rob McElhenney (now simply Rob Mac) completed their takeover of a club languishing in the National League. The knockout blow would be playing Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League in 2027-28 and the manager, Phil Parkinson, accepts there is expectation on Wrexham to complete their remarkable rise through the divisions next [...] “It is going to be a tough second season, we know that, but we feel there is more to come from the existing group. It was difficult last season with a lot of players coming in later and having to relocate to the area and settle as the season started, but they were great for us and I feel there is more to come this season.”

items.title: Footballer baby name trend takes off after 2026 World Cup: Here’s the most popular choice
items.summary:
The naming phenomenon accelerated during Norway's impressive World Cup campaign, with families embracing both the surname "Haaland" and the footballer's full name.

You may also like
Continue reading

According to Euronews, official registry figures show that 468 people in Peru now carry the surname Haaland, while 91 newborns have been registered with the full name "Erling Haaland."

Erling did not pick up the phone for Tom© Eurasia Sport Images [...] The Haaland naming trend illustrates how quickly sporting success can become part of everyday culture. A tournament lasting just a few weeks has already left a permanent mark on hundreds of Peruvian birth certificates.

As new football stars emerge during future World Cups, similar naming waves could easily follow.

READ MORE

World’s oldest soccer ball makes historic U.S. debut at FIFA World Cup and might belong to a woman [...] The FIFA World Cup has always inspired unforgettable moments, but in Peru, one of its biggest impacts is showing up on birth certificates. As Norway's Erling Haaland delivered standout performances at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, hundreds of Peruvian parents honored the striker by naming their newborns after him.

According to Peru's National Registry of Identification and Civil Status (RENIEC), the World Cup sparked a noticeable rise in Haaland-inspired names.

items.title: World Cup fuels tourism: Norway benefits from Haaland and Viking trend
items.summary:
Norway's image success is driven above all by its national team and its biggest star, Erling Haaland. Analysis by the Institute of Media Monitoring shows that during the World Cup the striker recorded the biggest growth in Instagram followers of any player at the tournament - an increase of 31.9 million users. [...] Experts point out that the way he communicated played a key role. Instead of professionally choreographed content, Haaland posted short behind-the-scenes videos from the national team camp, showed everyday situations and took a relaxed, self-deprecating approach to his own image. [...] The Norwegian case shows that major modern sporting events are becoming much more than just competition on the pitch. When the emotions of fans, social media and authentic heroes of the action are skilfully harnessed, they can effectively build a country's brand, boost its recognition and encourage tourists to plan trips.
